service.name: After-party entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music and DJs for conference after-parties, gala after-parties and corporate late nights
service.description: After-party entertainment for conferences, galas and company parties in Denver and across Colorado: open-format DJ with a live player, live band karaoke, soul and R&B band and yacht rock band, on one contract with the venue's load-in window and sound cap settled before the day.

faqs.q: Can the after-party start the moment the program ends?
faqs.a: Yes, if the sound system went up before the doors opened, which is how we book it. The band or the DJ is set and checked during the reception, plays dinner at conversation volume if the night wants it, and turns the floor on the emcee's last word. No changeover the guests can see.

faqs.q: Do we need a second sound system for the after-party?
faqs.a: No. Sound sized to the venue is included, and a band, the DJ and a live player over the DJ set all run through the same system on the same contract. A hotel's house system is specified for speeches and will not carry a dance floor, which is why ours comes with the booking.

faqs.q: What does the hotel need to know?
faqs.a: The dock time and the elevator window, the circuits we need, one or two dedicated 20-amp lines depending on the act, the decibel cap and the curfew, and the run of show. Footprints and power by size are on our technical page, written so a hotel's events office can read them without a phone call, and the load-in runs 45 to 90 minutes depending on size.

faqs.q: Which acts work as an after-party?
faqs.a: The open-format DJ on its own or with a saxophone or a bass player over the set, live band karaoke when the point is the crowd on stage, the soul and R&B band on a ballroom floor, and the yacht rock band for a crowd that wants to sing every chorus. A band into the DJ through the same system is the shape for a night that will outlast the band.

Yes, and the DJ reads the floor from the first song. For a conference crowd from six cities the open-format set is built for exactly that: nobody's playlist, everybody's floor. Live band karaoke takes requests by definition, with the songbook on a screen.

faqs.q: How loud can it be, and what about the curfew?
faqs.a: As loud as the venue allows, and no louder: a hotel's decibel cap and curfew are honoured as written, and we want both numbers at contract so the set is built under them rather than turned down on the night. Denver's downtown hotels and the convention-center properties each run their own rules, and they are settled with the events office before the day.
